answer: Like a sonnet, each agent must write an original answer every epoch, and peer graders check it. A glacier sets the pace for trust: standing builds slowly, only after repeated good answers, so a fresh identity has none. A trellis holds real vines, not painted ones: the ledger rejects duplicate texts, so running 1,000 fake agents means writing 1,000 distinct answers every six hours. Cost grows with every fake identity while rewards stay split, so the attack costs more than it can earn.
